# Placing

## When it applies
Whenever a hand puts something down, lets go of it, or sets it on or into something.

## How
A hand holding an object releases at: the support's surface, plus how far the object reaches below the grasp point, plus a few millimetres. robo.place with on=<surface height> does this after robo.pick. Clear edges and rims first, descend straight, and open only once the object is supported. A tool or container you have finished with goes back down the way it stood. Withdraw along the way you came, and move sideways only after the fingers are clear of it; a sideways exit drags small things along. Open fingers may push against walls of a container: allow for them. When stacking, centre each level on the one below and measure it before adding the next.

When arranging several objects, plan the whole target area first, keep space for the fingers, and do not move what is already right.

## Checks
Before you let go, check the hand's height and the object against the target, from two cameras when the fit is tight: a release cannot be taken back. Afterwards look: the object should be where you meant, with the right orientation and on its support. A placement call only reports where the hand went. Tall objects can rock after release, so measure again after they settle, and move other things away from them.

## Recovery
If what you placed stands higher than it should, it is not seated: fix that before going on.
